posts.cooked:
Hey everyone, just a quick reminder about how we’re handling the “solved” tag in this community. When you’re posting about a bug that’s been fixed, or a question that’s been answered, please make sure to actually use the [solved] tag in the title. It keeps things super clear and helps others find solutions without digging through tons of posts.

Also, if your issue turns out to be a duplicate of an earlier thread, try to link back to the original discussion and mark yours with [duplicate]. This way the conversations stay organized, and we avoid clutter.

One more thing—if you’re discussing something related to the remaster or any updates that patch out previous problems, tagging those appropriately helps us track which fixes were included in the new version. Keeping these conventions helps us all stay on the same page and makes the forum a better place to find info quickly. Thanks!

Hey everyone, just chiming in to say I really appreciate the clear tagging rules laid out here. It makes it so much easier to keep track of which issues have been resolved without having to dig through multiple replies. I’ve noticed a few threads where people forgot to add the [solved] tag after the fix was confirmed, so hopefully this reminder helps cut down on that.

Also, quick tip for those posting about remaster-related bugs: if the issue was already known from the original version, tagging it as [duplicate] before marking [solved] can help prevent repeated reports and keep things tidy. It’s great to have these conventions nailed down since the community keeps growing and the backlog of reports can get overwhelming.

Thanks again for putting this up! Looking forward to smoother discussions and quicker bug resolutions with everyone on the same page.
